To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the yeast cell cycle is driven by the periodic formation and disassembly of complexes, which are regulated through targeted protein degradation and phosphorylation.
the cell cycle can be described as a series of dynamic complexes and that these complexes consist of both constitutively and periodically expressed subunits.

most cell cycle complexes consist of both constitutively and periodically expressed proteins and that the former control the activity of cell cycle complexes by a mechanism of “just-in-time” assembly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics and regulation of protein complexes and their role in the cell cycle.
the analysis of dynamic protein complexes during the cell cycle.
the dynamics of protein-protein interactions during the cell cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temporal cell cycle network is a dynamic network of dynamic complexes.
the cell cycle network is composed of a set of modules, each with a specific function, which are controlled by the cell cycle machinery.
cell cycle control involves a combination of temporal and spatial regulation of the cell cycle network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the majority of complexes in the cell cycle are composed of both periodically and non-periodically expressed proteins, which suggests that complex formation is a mechanism for temporal control of complex activity during the cell cycle.
the majority of complexes are composed of both periodic and constitutive subunits, and the former regulate the complex activity through a mechanism of just in time assembly.

most complexes consist not only of periodically and constitutvely expressed subunits, but also of subunits that are regulated by degradation and Cdc28p-mediated phosphorylation, thereby controlling complex activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell cycle is a complex dynamic process that involves a large number of interactions and regulatory mechanisms, which together ensure proper cell division.
the temporal context of protein interactions can provide a powerful means to infer regulatory mechanisms.
the cell cycle is not just a series of periodic processes, but also involves a dynamic assembly of protein complexes that is regulated by a combination of temporal and spatial mechanisms.
